rationales: Electronic configuration was not the basis of Mendeleev’s table.
Atomic number was used as the basis of the modern periodic table.
Mendeleev arranged elements mainly by increasing atomic mass.
Subshell completion was not the basis of Mendeleev’s table.
Mass number is not the organizing basis of the long-form periodic table.
Mendeleev’s postulate does not determine the modern table’s arrangement.
The long-form periodic table is arranged by increasing atomic number.
Atomic mass was the basis of Mendeleev’s table, not the long-form table.
A triple covalent bond does not involve only three electrons.
Four electrons make a double covalent bond, not a triple bond.
A triple covalent bond consists of three shared pairs, or six electrons.
Eight electrons are not involved in a triple covalent bond.
A single line represents a single covalent bond.
Two parallel lines represent a double covalent bond.
Three parallel lines represent a triple covalent bond.
An arrow is used to represent a coordinate covalent bond.
Rubber is generally classified as an amorphous solid.
Plastic is generally classified as an amorphous solid.
Glucose forms a crystalline solid, so it is not amorphous.
Glass is an amorphous solid.
Chromium’s oxidation number is not +7 in K₂Cr₂O₇.
+14 is the total oxidation number of both chromium atoms, not one atom.
Each chromium atom has oxidation number +6 in K₂Cr₂O₇.
Chromium’s oxidation number is not +2 in K₂Cr₂O₇.
Carbon is not the lustrous non-metal intended here.
Phosphorus is generally dull, not lustrous.
Sulphur is generally dull, not lustrous.
Iodine is a lustrous non-metal.
Goldstein discovered canal rays, rather than identifying the proton as a particle.
J. J. Thomson discovered the electron.
Bohr developed a model of the atom and did not discover the proton.
Rutherford is credited with discovering the proton.
H₂ contains two atoms and is diatomic.
O₂ contains two atoms and is diatomic.
Cl₂ contains two atoms and is diatomic.
CO₂ contains three atoms and is triatomic.
The fourth and fifth periods are not classified as short periods.
The fourth and fifth periods are classified as long periods, not normal periods.
The fourth and fifth periods are called long periods.
The sixth and seventh periods are called very long periods.
Sugar solution does not produce ions in solution and is a non-electrolyte.
Sulphuric acid solution produces ions and is an electrolyte.
Lime solution contains ions and conducts electricity, so it is an electrolyte.
Sodium chloride solution contains ions and is an electrolyte.
HCl has a single bond, whereas O₂ has a double bond.
N₂ has a triple bond, whereas O₂ has a double bond.
C₂H₄ and O₂ both contain double covalent bonds.
C₂H₂ has a triple bond, whereas O₂ has a double bond.
Covalent bonding generally occurs between non-metal atoms.
An electronegative element and an electropositive element typically form an ionic bond.
Polar covalent bonding involves unequal sharing between covalently bonded atoms.
Coordinate covalent bonding requires one atom to donate both shared electrons.
Air is generally a homogeneous mixture of gases.
Rock is heterogeneous because its components are not uniformly distributed.
Gasoline is generally a homogeneous mixture.
Iodine is an element, not a mixture.
Thomson proposed the plum pudding model of the atom.
Goldstein is known for discovering canal rays, not proposing this model.
Bohr proposed a model with electrons in defined energy levels.
Chadwick discovered the neutron.
